title: Bloom Energy Stock Sinks Despite Record Revenue and a Stellar Outlook. Is It Time to Buy?
detail:
Bloom Energy Stock Sinks Despite Record Revenue and a Stellar Outlook. Is It Time to Buy?
Neha Chamaria, The Motley Fool

BE
ORCL
NVDA

Trading disclosure

Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE) delivered another blowout quarter, smashing estimates and growing profits faster than sales. Yet, its stock plunged after earnings and was down more than 12% as of Friday noon.

The company sells solid-oxide fuel cell servers that turn natural gas into electricity right at a customer's site. Artificial intelligence (AI) data centers desperately need that because the existing grid needs years to build additional capacity.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Bloom Energy can bypass the grid and swiftly deliver clean, reliable, 24/7 power to hyperscalers and data center operators. It delivered a complete fuel-cell system to Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) in 55 days last year. The tech giant was so impressed that it expanded its partnership for up to 2.8 gigawatts (GW) earlier this year.

So, what is happening with Bloom Energy stock? Why is it dropping like a rock – down 30% in one month, as of this writing?

Image source: Getty Images.

A bumper quarter and 2027 outlook

Revenue soared 138% year over year to a record $1.2 billion in the third quarter. Product sales, the fuel cell systems Bloom Energy ships to customers, topped $1 billion in sales in a single quarter for the first time.

Profit grew even faster. Adjusted operating margin jumped to 23.1% from 8.9% as revenue more than doubled while operating expenses rose only 26%. CFO Simon Edwards added that operating income in this single quarter surpassed what Bloom earned in all of 2025.

Then management raised its full-year revenue outlook for the third time this year. It now expects 2026 revenue of $4.5 billion, or about 122% growth.

Here's the kicker: Earlier in the year, Bloom Energy was guiding for a "humble" 60% revenue growth for the year. It has more than doubled its trajectory in just a couple of quarters.

So what's hurting the stock? The only metric I could find that may have miffed investors is cash burn. Bloom Energy posted negative free cash flow of $181 million in Q3.

Should investors worry? Hardly, because context is everything.

Is Bloom Energy stock a buy?

Demand is exploding, so Bloom Energy spent $153 million last quarter to scale up capacity as fast as possible. Data centers are built in phases, and Bloom is ready with its servers at each phase so operators don't have to wait.

That speed is everything for data centers.

1 software stock worth your attention and 2 we brush off

From commerce to culture, software is digitizing every aspect of our lives. This secular theme has materialized in superior earnings growth and stock price performance for most SaaS companies, and over the last six months, the industry's 54.6% return has topped the S&P 500 by 45.5 percentage points.

Nevertheless, investors should tread carefully as AI will commoditize many software products, and backing the wrong horse could result in hefty losses. Keeping that in mind, here is one software stock poised to generate sustainable market-beating returns and two we would avoid.

Two software stocks to sell:
UiPath (PATH)

Market Cap: $7.26 billion

Starting with robotic process automation (RPA) and evolving into a comprehensive automation powerhouse, UiPath (NYSE:PATH) provides an AI-powered business automation platform that enables organizations to create software robots that mimic human actions to streamline repetitive tasks and processes.

Why Does PATH Worry Us?

ARR growth averaged a weak 11.7% over the last year, suggesting that competition is pulling some attention away from its software

Estimated sales growth of 8.2% for the next 12 months implies demand will slow from its two-year trend

Extended payback periods on sales investments suggest the company's platform isn't resonating enough to drive efficient sales conversions

UiPath's stock price of $13.83 implies a valuation ratio of 3.9x forward price-to-sales. Read our free research report to see why you should think twice about including PATH in your portfolio, it's free.

Oracle (ORCL)

Market Cap: $380.6 billion

Starting as a database company in 1977 and now powering mission-critical systems across the globe, Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) provides enterprise software and hardware products and services that help businesses manage their information technology needs.

Why Does ORCL Give Us Pause?

Annual sales growth of 11.9% over the last five years lagged behind its software peers as its large revenue base made it difficult to generate incremental demand

Cash-burning history makes us doubt the long-term viability of its business model

Short cash runway increases the probability of a capital raise that dilutes existing shareholders

Oracle is trading at $125.06 per share, or 3.9x forward price-to-sales. Dive into our free research report to see why there are better opportunities than ORCL.

One software stock to watch:
HubSpot (HUBS)

Market Cap: $13.32 billion

Born from the idea that traditional interruptive marketing was becoming less effective, HubSpot (NYSE:HUBS) provides an integrated platform that helps businesses attract, engage, and manage customer relationships through marketing, sales, service, and content management tools.

title: Oracle vs. Alibaba: Which Cloud Stock Holds the Edge Right Now?
detail:
Oracle vs. Alibaba: Which Cloud Stock Holds the Edge Right Now?
Vasundhara Sawalka
Fri, October 23, 2026 at 6:02 AM MST 5 min read
ORCL
BABA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Oracle ORCL and Alibaba Group BABA have each repositioned as artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure providers, pairing massive data center buildouts with proprietary software. Oracle leverages Oracle Cloud Infrastructure ("OCI"), its database franchise and Fusion applications, while Alibaba combines Alibaba Cloud, its Qwen model family and in-house T-Head chips under one full-stack strategy.

Both companies are spending aggressively on capital expenditure (capex) to meet AI compute demand that outstrips supply, making funding discipline and monetization pace critical differentiators now.

Let's delve deep and closely compare the fundamentals of the two stocks to determine which one is a better investment now.

The Case for ORCL Stock

Oracle's biggest strength is contracted visibility. Remaining performance obligations (RPO) reached $664 billion at the end of first-quarter fiscal 2027, and management expects roughly half to convert into revenue over the next 36 months. Oracle booked more than $30 billion of new AI cloud contracts, mostly structured through customer prepayments or bring-your-own-hardware arrangements that require no incremental cash from Oracle, easing funding concerns and supporting a self-funding growth model.

Fleet economics remain highly encouraging for long-term profitability. GPU utilization stood at 97.9%, and capacity up for renewal was re-contracted at a 20% premium. Multicloud database revenues grew 353% as Oracle completed its planned Azure and AWS regional expansion, reaching 70 multicloud database regions. The applications portfolio adds diversification, with Fusion growing 14% and AI agents increasingly embedded across customer workflows, deepening customer stickiness.

Recent announcements strengthen the AI software layer. In October 2026, Oracle added xAI's Grok 4.6 and 4.7 models and a Smart Model Router to OCI Enterprise AI. On Oct. 21, it unveiled AI Agent Studio for Industry Applications, a no-code and low-code environment for building industry-specific AI agents.

For fiscal 2027, Oracle raised its revenue outlook to at least $90 billion, implying 34% growth, and expects non-GAAP EPS of $8.10. For the second quarter, it guides total revenue growth of 30-34% and cloud revenue growth of 65-71%. Challenges include a fiscal 2027 capex projection of $90-$95 billion, negative free cash flow, a completed $20 billion equity issuance and air-permitting and power-delivery hurdles at certain data center sites.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ORCL's fiscal 2027 earnings is currently pegged at $8.13 per share. The estimate implies 6.55% year-over-year earnings growth.

Oil prices climbing above $113 and renewed worries around energy security have pushed investors back toward companies with clear leadership and accountability. When the founder is still at the helm, incentives are often tightly aligned with long term performance, not the next quarter. This article looks at three founder driven US stocks from our curated universe that capture that mindset and explains why they may deserve a spot on your watchlist.

The three stocks highlighted here offer a compelling starting point if you want exposure to founder led businesses where leadership is personally tied to long term outcomes. However, if you want the standouts, these 30 top founder-led companies are the most outstanding.

Tesla (TSLA)

Tesla is the clearest expression of the Founder-Led Companies theme in this list. Elon Musk still sets the direction, and the business model reflects that, with a focus on electric vehicles, software and energy systems that try to reshape how drivers think about cars and power.

Tesla designs and sells electric vehicles alongside energy storage and solar products, led by founder Elon Musk whose decisions closely shape product direction and long term ambition. The group has a market value of about US$1.53 trillion, reflecting how central Tesla has become to the listed EV and clean energy space.

"Tesla is pursuing a range of ambitious and, in some cases, speculative opportunities: AI leadership, robotaxis, humanoid robotics, and battery storage. While the company has achieved some success in energy storage, competition is intensifying there as well."

What matters most now is how one pressure behind those ambitions eventually feeds through to cash generation and long term shareholder returns.

That tension between bold bets and cash generation sits at the heart of the full narrative for Tesla. It lays out how Tesla's ambitions, risks and optionality could reshape the story from here.

NasdaqGS:TSLA 1-Year Stock Price Chart
Sweetgreen (SG)

Sweetgreen brings the founder-led idea into everyday life, with Jonathan Neman's early playbook on menu, digital ordering and new locations still shaping how the salad chain runs its restaurants and app. The group generated US$681.77 million from company-owned stores in the United States and carries a market value of about US$1.21 billion.

For investors focused on founder-driven stories, Sweetgreen offers a cleaner test case than many diversified groups because almost all of the business still flows through a single concept that blends healthy food with a heavy digital ordering tilt, and the next phase depends on how that formula lands with guests.
